_comment: Same-box A/B record for the P1 softmax-scale-fold change (jammi_kernels::ops::softmax's SoftmaxLastDimFused::with_scale folding 1/sqrt(head_dim) into the fused softmax op). The two arms differ by EXACTLY ONE thing: `base` is the training arm BEFORE this change -- ModernBertAttention::forward built a `scores / sqrt(head_dim)` Op::Affine node (a full [batch*3, heads, seq, seq] retained tape tensor per layer -- see below for the *3) and then called the fused softmax with scale=1.0; `tip` is the training arm AFTER -- the same 1/sqrt(head_dim) folded directly into SoftmaxLastDimFused via with_scale, so that Op::Affine node is never constructed at all. Nothing else moved: same model config, same LoRA config, same dtype, same step/warmup/seed. peak_vram_bytes is the tier's device-total-minus-baseline (nvidia-smi/pool high-water mark across the whole run), NOT a live/allocator-delta reading -- the same convention documented in finetune_step_reference.json's own _comment. softmax_fused_dispatches/lora_epilogue_fused_dispatches are identical on both legs and all three rows (700 and 2800 respectively, 0 eager fallbacks on either arm) because this change alters WHEN scale is applied, not WHETHER the fused softmax or LoRA epilogue kernels are admitted -- confirming the two arms really do differ only by the Affine-node removal, not by a change in kernel admission. B_eff is NOT the three LoRA target modules -- this run's LoRA targets never touch the attention module's own leading batch axis. Mechanism: with `batched_forward` on, finetune_step.rs's step loop concatenates the anchor/positive/negative triplet blocks along dim 0 BEFORE the single encoder.forward call (`Tensor::cat(&[&blocks[0], &blocks[1], &blocks[2]], 0)`, finetune_step.rs:454), so the tensor ModernBertAttention actually sees has a LEADING batch axis of `3 * batch`, not `batch` -- that is B_eff. Predicted per-row saving from dropping one [B_eff, H, S, S] bf16 Op::Affine node per layer: B_eff * H * S * S * 2 bytes/elem * 28 layers (ModernBERT-large). DISCLOSED HONESTLY, all three rows, not just the favorable one: b8-s512-d0 (B_eff=24, S=512): predicted 24*16*512*512*2*28 = 5,637,144,576 B saved; MEASURED 77,462,503,424 - 71,758,249,984 = 5,704,253,440 B saved -- 2 allocator pool blocks (2*33,554,432 B) more than predicted, the same order of magnitude. b16-s128-d0 (B_eff=48, S=128): predicted 48*16*128*128*2*28 = 704,643,072 B saved; MEASURED 33,237,762,048 - 32,566,673,408 = 671,088,640 B saved -- exactly ONE allocator pool block (33,554,432 B) less than predicted; this is the calibration row, showing the mechanism's prediction lands within a single pool-block quantum of the measurement when the predicted effect is large relative to one block. b8-s128-d0 (B_eff=24, S=128) is the CONTRARY row, stated plainly rather than omitted: predicted 24*16*128*128*2*28 = 352,321,536 B saved, but MEASURED tip is 23,775,412,224 - 23,741,857,792 = 33,554,432 B *more* than base (exactly one pool block WORSE, not better) -- at this row the predicted effect (352 MB) is small enough, and one pool block (32 MiB) coarse enough, that allocator pool granularity/fragmentation from unrelated transient allocations across the run dominates the signal; the Affine-node-removal mechanism is real (confirmed by the other two rows and by the dispatch-counter identity above) but this one row's peak-VRAM delta is not a clean readout of it. RECORD, never gate (heterogeneous-fleet doctrine, same as finetune_step_reference.json).

provenance.base_disposition: P1 absent (branch base: training arm builds an Op::Affine scores/sqrt(head_dim) node before calling the fused softmax with scale=1.0)
provenance.tip_disposition: P1 present (1/sqrt(head_dim) folded into SoftmaxLastDimFused via with_scale; no Op::Affine node built)
provenance.b_eff_mechanism: batched_forward concatenates the anchor/positive/negative triplet along dim 0 before the single encoder.forward call (`Tensor::cat(&[&blocks[0], &blocks[1], &blocks[2]], 0)`, finetune_step.rs:454), so B_eff = 3 * batch, not related to lora_targets
